items.reason: The stated defect is placement/coupling: the behavior is not a specific option for this command and is not executed after the handle command, and omitting the change leaves that arrangement exactly as the reviewer objects to it. Terra rejected the render solely because the source used first-person hedging and a question mark ("I personally think it would make more sense ... ?"), even though the candidate keeps the hedge as a fact ("I personally think that would make more sense") while stating the target behavior.

The defect is the ambiguous message text "file(s)" when the count is rows, and omitting the edit leaves the misleading message in the code, confirmed by the source's inline `suggestion` block containing the replacement line. Terra rejected the render solely because the source verb was "consider clarifying the message", which under the frozen rubric does not make target behavior optional.

The defect is undocumented rationale for writing an empty manifest, and omitting the comment leaves the reason unrecorded; required documentation is author work, and the source's `suggestion` block supplies the exact comment text. Terra rejected the render solely because the source said "consider adding a comment explaining why an empty manifest is still created", i.e. on modal/politeness grammar rather than behavior.

The defect is N+1 loading — a `DESCRIBE` plus `INSERT ... SELECT` per URL — and omitting either branch leaves the loop and its unexplained rationale in place, so both branches are author work. Terra's flagged failure is not modal-based and is real: the source's "a one-line comment explaining that would help future readers" is reduced in the candidate to "or add a one-line comment if strict `NOT NULL` typing on `{table}_instances` prevents that fast path", dropping the stated benefit to future readers.

The defect is that the test asserts on the "Could not find file or directory" message for an existing-but-unsupported `.txt` path, which is misleading and obscures the unsupported-extension intent; omitting the change leaves the misleading assertion, and the source's `suggestion` block gives the `pytest.raises(Exception)` replacement. Terra rejected the render solely on the word "Consider", even though the candidate preserves both the alternative structure and the explicit longer-term marker ("or, as a longer-term change, make `expand_paths` raise a distinct exception or message").

The defect is a slug mismatch (`qwen` → `alibaba`) that will make HAL exports inconsistent and may split Qwen models across two developer directories; omitting the change leaves that inconsistency, and the source's `suggestion` block sets `"qwen": "qwen"`. Terra rejected the render solely because the source said "Consider using `qwen` here (or otherwise aligning ...)", while the candidate preserves the same or-alternative as "Please use `qwen` here, or otherwise align the mapping and overrides".

No confirmed defect is asserted — "This might end up being a bottleneck" and "It may be worth it to abstract" accept current behavior, so omission resolves nothing and the candidate's "An optional follow-up is to abstract" rendering is correct. Terra's flagged loss is nonetheless real: the source's first-person provenance "I've handled this in a few ways in the past: simple wrappers" and "And module level globals" becomes the impersonal "Similar approaches include simple wrappers ... and module-level globals", dropping the reviewer's stated prior use of those approaches.

The [medium] defect is that reusing an output directory creates duplicate logical evaluations because `save_evaluation_log()` mints a new UUID filename per call; omitting the fix leaves output non-idempotent despite stable `evaluation_id` values. Terra rejected the render solely on the modal "An adapter-owned aggregate and sidecar can be replaced as one set", ignoring that the same paragraph states a hard requirement ("The sidecar needs a fresh write").

The [medium] defect is that `expand_paths()` returns only the named file, so `abc.json.gz` escapes the one-variant rule when the caller names only `abc.json`; omitting the change leaves that validation hole open. Terra rejected the render solely on the modal "Collision discovery can inspect same-parent, same-stem variants", although the candidate also preserves the boundary "while keeping payload validation limited to the requested files".

The [high] defect is that new instance records keep `instance_level_eval_0.2.2` while the existing 0.2.2 model rejects `modality` and null `is_correct`, and the old aggregate model discards the new modality under an unchanged identifier; omitting the version bump leaves records mismatched with their declared schema. Terra rejected the render solely on the modal "can move to new identifiers together", while the candidate preserves the mitigating fact "The extension is well scoped".

The [medium] defect is that a handled fetch, conversion, or write failure still reaches `Done!` and exits 0, so automation can treat a partial dataset as complete; omitting the change leaves the false success signal. Terra rejected the render solely on the conditional modal "both outcomes can feed a final status that `__main__` propagates", even though the candidate keeps both the condition ("if this entry point keeps independent work") and the alternative ("Delegation may remove this duplicate path").

The [medium] defect is that Pydantic `ValidationError` is outside the catch tuple, so one malformed benchmark aborts all later targets instead of joining the partial-run report; omitting the change leaves that failure mode. Terra rejected the render solely on the modal "That error can stay inside the per-benchmark boundary", which under the frozen rubric does not make the fix optional.

The [medium] defect is that `float()` accepts booleans, NaN, infinity, out-of-range Pass^k values, and negative costs on a path reachable by local replay and custom sources; omitting the checks leaves values outside the source contract accepted. Terra rejected the render solely on modal phrasing ("Pass metrics can use finite inclusive 0–100 checks", "Cost can use a finite non-negative check"), while the candidate preserves the scope fact that current official submissions are valid.

The [medium] defect is that the serializer declares no output union, so Pydantic describes the bound as number or null although `model_dump_json()` can emit `"Infinity"` or `"-Infinity"`; omitting the change leaves the published schema inaccurate. Terra rejected the render solely on the modal "Each bound can expose an accurate serialization contract", which does not make the correction optional.

The [medium] defect is that metadata and the three CSVs are separate reads from mutable `main`, so one export can mix revisions and metadata errors collapse to an empty object with the promised version anchor omitted; omitting the pin leaves provenance unsound. Terra rejected the render solely on the modal "Resolving one Hugging Face dataset revision can pin every live read", while the candidate correctly leaves the explicit boundary unchanged ("The dataset revision and manifest `source_git_commit` can remain separate provenance fields").

The defect is verified: `re.IGNORECASE` lets `<uuid>_Samples.jsonl` pass `check_path_structure` while `check_instance_companion` returns no errors, so it skips every companion rule; omitting the change leaves that hole open. Terra rejected the render solely on the gerund phrasing "dropping `re.IGNORECASE` closes the hole with no loss", although the source states the enabling fact ("Publishers only emit lowercase names") and the candidate preserves it along with the `.JSON`/`unsupported_extension` parenthetical.
